name: VideoScribe
tagline: Desktop and web tool for making whiteboard-style animated explainer videos where a hand draws your images and text.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The signature effect, a hand drawing an SVG stroke by stroke, is a solved browser trick: stroke-dasharray animation plus a hand sprite riding getPointAtLength along each path. An agent can get you a scene timeline, text-to-handwriting, camera pans, and a webm export in a weekend. What it cannot hand you is the library of thousands of licensed hand-drawn images, the handwriting fonts that actually look drawn, or the export pipeline that reliably spits out clean MP4 at 1080p. You will spend more time sourcing art than writing code, and your first ten videos will look like a tech demo rather than an explainer. Fine if you make two videos a year and own your assets; annoying if you need volume.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you assemble scenes from your own SVGs and text, then watch a hand sprite draw each element in order and record the result to a video file.
requirements: Your own SVG artwork with sensible stroke paths, or a source for it
A handwriting-style font you have rights to
Chromium for MediaRecorder capture, ffmpeg installed if you want MP4
whatYouLose: The bundled library of licensed hand-drawn images and the search that makes it usable
Royalty-free music and voiceover recording in the same tool
Reliable MP4/1080p export instead of a browser screen capture that drops frames
Polished easing, hand variants, and camera moves that make the effect read as professional
Raster image support: converting a PNG into a convincing drawn stroke order is a whole separate problem
moatNotes: The animation engine is a weekend. The asset library and the licensing behind it are the product.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because nobody buys this software for the stroke animation, they buy it for the fact that typing "handshake" gives them a drawn handshake they are legally allowed to put in a client video. The hand-drawing effect is cheap to replicate and the art pipeline is not. Add the music library, the one-click export that does not require explaining MediaRecorder to a marketing manager, and the fact that whiteboard video is usually a deadline job, and a subscription is the cheap option for anyone making these regularly.
notes: Build the engine for fun, then realise your bottleneck was always the drawings.
prompt:
Build a local whiteboard-animation video maker called HandDraw. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable: Vite + TypeScript, vanilla DOM and inline SVG, no React, no canvas library. Everything runs from `npm run dev` on localhost.

Data model: a project is a single JSON file, `project.json`, holding an ordered list of scenes. Each scene is one of:
- `svg`: a path to an SVG file in `assets/`, with x, y, scale, and drawSeconds
- `text`: a string rendered in a handwriting font, drawn character path by character path if the font allows, otherwise revealed left to right with the hand sprite following
- `hold`: a pause of N seconds

Animation engine:
- For each SVG, collect all `path`, `line`, `polyline` and `circle` elements in document order, convert to paths, and animate each with stroke-dasharray / stroke-dashoffset from hidden to fully drawn
- A hand sprite PNG (`assets/hand.png`, ship a crude placeholder and a README note telling the user to replace it) is positioned every frame at `path.getPointAtLength(progress)` with a configurable pen-tip offset
- Fills appear instantly at the moment that element finishes being outlined
- Between scenes, animate the SVG viewBox to pan and zoom to the next scene's bounding box over 0.8s with ease-in-out

UI: left panel is the scene list with add, delete, reorder and per-scene duration; right side is the stage at 1920x1080 scaled to fit; bottom is play, pause, scrub, and total runtime.

Export: a Record button that runs the timeline at real time, captures the stage with `MediaRecorder` on a `captureStream` of a canvas mirror of the SVG, and saves a .webm. Then print the exact ffmpeg command to convert to MP4. Do not pretend the webm is broadcast quality; say so in the README.

Explicitly out of scope: any bundled art or music library, voiceover recording, raster-to-stroke conversion, collaboration, undo history beyond a single step.

Ship: README with setup, the project.json schema, one three-scene example project, and two placeholder SVGs.
